Boy am I ever glad to be home all clean and warm, sitting in my favorite chair with a cold beer. Home, you never really realize how much you miss it till you travel a bunch. Heck even once is plenty if you're gone far and long enough.

Sit back now kiddo, does this ol' man ever got a bit of a tale cookin up. So this latest job I took had a small crew, real small. 15 guys total and that ain't nothin' for me to take care of. We hit up a little planet near the ol' Tera system and boy was it ever dusty as sin. Parched land spread before myself and the crewmen. Wind scribed sandy desert stretched far as the eye could see, small pocks in the landscape. Cracks in the what seemed like old lake beds peeled off in all directions. Spiderwebs in the sea of sand beige.

Well boy howdy did we ever have a little bit of a thing. Small scouting party was sent out to check out the surrounding area. Those boys came back in quite the state of shock and awe. Meeting with the command of the expedition in a small tent, away from us lower ranking and enlisted men, we cooks don't get lots of roam other than what is put on the menu and happening in our kitchen.

Story around camp was that they found some other camps not too far from ours. Slavers. Case you live on a comet somewhere in the depths of deep outer space, slavers are easily one of the most unwanted things to come across in the space of many galaxies. They're brutal, and unforgiving taking lives if they feel like it or even if they don't. I would even classify them as detestable, but that's just me.

So anyways the command, his bloody highness decided in his almighty wisdom to go out and “Rid this small planet of their presence”. I got myself a little bit of heat to pack so I was set in case they didn't come back. Always do, rather have it and not need it than not have it and need it I always say. My dad taught me that when I was naught but knee high.

First out was a little troop of 5 men, leaving 10 and myself back at camp. Those poor boys never came back, no comms transmission even. The last 10 left about 3 days after, only about 40 hours on this planet. They we're within radio contact of me for a while, a good while at that. 30 hours had passed by the time I lost contact with 'em and I got worried. My arsenal was enough to protect me but that was about it. Side arm pistol; a colt 1911 that my father gave to me a family heirloom nowadays, Rifle; standard issue military style AR 8900 energy rifle. Its pretty good, accurate as hell and fires a small lazer burst, I taped my favorite knife to the end as a makeshift bayonet. That was it, I had about 60 rounds of pistol ammo, and about 300 rifle ammo, plenty for the cook I guess but I would have been happier off that rock.

No contact ever came from the 9 crewmen or the commander, not a whisper. Searching in a panic after many hours of waiting for a radio to a station was in vain, the commander took it. That arrogant son of a bitch took the only satlink in the camp, leaving me stranded without comms to a station. Fan-freakin-tastic.

In the end I wound up getting all my gear in a rucksack and lugging it along to where I could find the camp of slavers, there were a few lookouts hanging out in some ruins long forgotten. Dust sifted down through the bricks and stones that made up the high arch of the entrance to a catacombs weaving about in the depths of the planet.

Once I opened fire on the lookouts they came out in leaps and bounds, pouring from the stone like ants to honey. Sounds of gunfire led them in droves and I fired at them all, until no movement was left. Making my way into the catacombs I heard sounds of people still, moaning and begging, pleading with their respective gods. The cool air under the stone felt good after the scorching heat of the desert.

I found cage lined caves, giant ones big enough to house a city the caves loomed into the darkness full of cages. People were in them, as soon as I blasted the first lock they flowed out like a fluid. I handed my rifle over removing my knife quickly and keeping it about myself. A few made their way out and returned with keys and weapons to open the remaining cages and a few paid respect to me for doing what my crew had seemingly dissipated doing.

What happened to them? Did they get killed or taken by the slavers? I never did find any of them or their remains before I left. I found a satlink on one of the now dead slavers and called in a pickup, enough for at least 500 I guessed not only hours later did a giant ship come into orbit, it was just visible from the planets surface emitting dropships like larvae into the sky.

Picking us up and dashing us from that planet, I couldn't help but wonder what happened to my crew, and loathe the debrief to come. In the end everyone got on board safely and honestly its nice to be home. Keep your loved ones close, real close kids. You never know what could be around the corner. But hey at least my leg don't hurt no more. Eat well kids, be safe.
